source.title: Similarity and Matching of Neural Network Representations
source.authors: A. Csiszárik; Péter Kőrösi-Szabó; Ákos K. Matszangosz; G. Papp; D. Varga

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests representation matchability and similarity with affine stitching and task performance, a conceptual alternative to direct representational-distance comparisons.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own stitching, similarity-index and width-sweep results. Values used only to choose hyperparameters, cited findings, and visualization examples without reported outcomes are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study measures how well independently initialised CNNs of the same architecture can be mapped onto each other with affine stitching layers, judged by task performance. It also tests whether CKA, R², CCA and SVCCA track that functional matchability. These results bear directly on V3, V4 and V6, and on V1 only through a same-architecture width sweep.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that same-architecture CNNs differing only in initialization are robustly matchable with a single affine stitching layer, at close to original performance. They find that similarity indices such as CKA are not necessarily indicative of stitched task performance, and that SVD variance does not match information content. They also find the relationship between representations is typically not combinatorial or sparse.
record.recipe_differences: Uses affine model stitching, task performance, and comparisons of CKA and other indices rather than reproducing the original sources' methods. The experiments mainly use same-architecture convolutional networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by stitching method, layer, rank, sparsity, network width, and similarity index. Direct matching is weaker than task-loss matching in several settings; CKA, the least-squares coefficient, CCA, and SVCCA behave differently during training.
record.problems: Experiments are restricted mainly to established convolutional vision architectures. Width is analysed only in isolation. The authors note that stitched performance is a lower bound because optimization can reach local minima. Many layerwise results appear only in figures, without tabulated exact values. The CelebA task has a high majority-class baseline.
record.rows_left_out: Layerwise values from Figures 6, 10–16 and the cross-layer sanity-check heatmaps were not individually transcribed. They are primarily additional initialization, connectivity, sparsity, weighted-matching, or layer-pair details beyond the central claim; some are only plotted. Their qualitative findings are summarized where stated in the text.

untested.parts: Different architectures, objectives, data or modalities; scale beyond a 1x–4x width sweep of a single ResNet-20; representational-distance measures as a function of scale.
Entirely untested: there is no vision–language or paired image-caption comparison.
Recurrence of specific features or units is not tested; only functional linear matchability and the sparsity of the stitching map are.
Cross-architecture stitching, relative representations and mapping without paired data.
Entirely untested; the feature visualizations come with no quantitative recurrence result.
Input distribution or out-of-distribution dependence, and neighbour-count settings of kNN-style measures.
Plateauing of alignment, and shared data or objectives as its cause.

missing.what: Table 2a layer 5b values: least squares 95.57%, Frankenstein 97.02%.
Worst stitch is after ResNet-20's first conv layer, still about 80% relative accuracy. No unmatchable cases were found across BN/no-BN and SGD/Adam.
Stitching from random initialization sometimes gets stuck in poor local minima; least-squares initialization is consistently good (Figures 6, 10).
Linear mode connectivity of stitching matrices fails on the first three Tiny-10 layers despite high accuracy.
Procrustes (orthogonal) matching equals least-squares accuracy on later layers.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 caption assignment is likely swapped in the extracted text. The prose says CelebA–CelebA stitches are close to 100%, and that ImageNet-to-CelebA shows about a 3% drop at high layers. That fits the column decreasing to 97.02% (labelled 2a), not the column near 100% (labelled 2b). If so, the condition labels of r15–r48 are reversed between same-task and cross-task. The verdicts hold either way, since both sets are high. CelebA's high majority baseline (87.63% relative) compresses all Inception values. r13/r14 are post-stitch CKA baselines, not raw cross-seed similarity. The paper is not an original source for any version. Convergent Learning (an original for V3) is only cited.

versions.untested_parts: Only a ResNet-20 width sweep is reported. The study does not test convergence across different architectures, objectives, datasets, or modalities, nor does it test whether scale increases representational-distance similarity measures.
No paired image-caption vision-language representation comparison.
The study tests functional stitchability, not whether particular features or shared subspaces recur across random seeds.
Tests affine stitching of convolutional networks. Does not test stitching across different architectures, relative representations, or unpaired-data mapping.
No recurrence of interpretable features or circuits is tested.
Compares similarity indices and task performance, but does not systematically vary input distributions, test out-of-distribution data, or sweep settings such as neighbour count.
Does not test whether shared data or objectives cause alignment, or whether alignment plateaus or remains incomplete as a general phenomenon.
